# File commands: upload, thumbnail upload/share, download, attachment url

## `fptctl attachment url`

Print the download URL of ATTACHMENT.

ATTACHMENT is an Attachment id, or the value of a file/link field as JSON. The library builds the URL without a request; opening it in a browser needs a signed-in session.

```text
fptctl attachment url [OPTIONS] ATTACHMENT
```

Library call: `Shotgun.get_attachment_download_url`.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl attachment url 941
```

## `fptctl download`

Download ATTACHMENT to a file or to stdout.

ATTACHMENT is an Attachment id, or the value of a file/link field as JSON, as find returns it. With -o PATH the file is written there and PATH is printed; with -o - the raw bytes go to stdout, for piping.

```text
fptctl download [OPTIONS] ATTACHMENT
```

Library call: `Shotgun.download_attachment`.

Options:

- `-o, --output PATH|-`: Write the file to PATH and print PATH, or write the raw bytes to stdout with '-'. [required]

Examples:

```shell
fptctl download 941 -o plate.mov
fptctl download '{"type": "Attachment", "id": 941}' -o - | shasum
```

## `fptctl thumbnail share`

Give every ENTITY the same thumbnail.

Each ENTITY is Type:123 or a JSON object. Give the image with --path, which uploads it once and shares it with the rest, or with --source, which shares the thumbnail another entity already has. A thumbnail the server is still processing cannot be shared yet (exit 5). Prints the Attachment id.

```text
fptctl thumbnail share [OPTIONS] ENTITY...
```

Library call: `Shotgun.share_thumbnail`.

Options:

- `--path FILE`: Upload this image and share it.
- `--source ENTITY`: Share this entity's thumbnail.
- `--filmstrip`: Share a filmstrip thumbnail.
- `--display-name TEXT`: The Attachment's display name.
- `--tag-list TEXT`: Tags for the Attachment, comma-separated.
- `--created-at YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`: The upload's creation time.
- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl thumbnail share Shot:1234 Shot:1235 --path thumb.png
fptctl thumbnail share Task:55 Task:56 --source Shot:1234
```

## `fptctl thumbnail upload`

Set the thumbnail of entity ID of TYPE from the image at PATH.

TYPE is an entity type, ID the entity's id and PATH a local image. With --filmstrip the image is a filmstrip, frames side by side, for scrubbing in the web UI. Prints the Attachment id the library returns.

```text
fptctl thumbnail upload [OPTIONS] TYPE ID PATH
```

Library call: `Shotgun.upload_filmstrip_thumbnail`, `Shotgun.upload_thumbnail`.

Options:

- `--filmstrip`: Upload a filmstrip thumbnail.
- `--display-name TEXT`: The Attachment's display name.
- `--tag-list TEXT`: Tags for the Attachment, comma-separated.
- `--created-at YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`: The upload's creation time.
- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl thumbnail upload Shot 1234 thumb.png
fptctl thumbnail upload Shot 1234 strip.png --filmstrip
```

## `fptctl upload`

Upload the file at PATH to entity ID of TYPE.

TYPE is an entity type, ID the entity's id and PATH a local file. With --field-name the file goes into that file/link field; without it, it is attached to the entity. Prints the new Attachment's id.

```text
fptctl upload [OPTIONS] TYPE ID PATH
```

Library call: `Shotgun.upload`.

Options:

- `--field-name TEXT`: The file/link field to hold the upload.
- `--display-name TEXT`: The Attachment's display name.
- `--tag-list TEXT`: Tags for the Attachment, comma-separated.
- `--created-at YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`: The upload's creation time.
- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl upload Shot 1234 plate.mov --field-name sg_uploaded_movie
fptctl upload Shot 1234 notes.pdf --display-name "Client notes" --tag-list review
```
